answer: An agent economy can weight marketplace votes by tokens locked in escrow, rather than by account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still buys only 100 tokens of influence, so a bridge that admits new agents does not create free voting power. To dominate, an attacker must acquire and lock more stake than honest participants, tying up capital for the lock period. The oasis of unlimited influence from free identities becomes a fable.
